simple.meaning: אָטַם (ʼâṭam) is a Hebrew action word meaning “to close (the lips or ears); by analology to contract (a window by bevelled jambs).” BibleIQ anchors the English reading to this source verb before comparing its uses.
simple.biblicalBackground: This action appears 8 times in 1 Kings, Psalms, Proverbs, Isaiah, Ezekiel, beginning at 1 Kings 6:4. The surrounding contexts include righteousness.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to אָטַם (H331) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Actions in Scripture show what people do, what God does, and how covenant faithfulness or rebellion is described. BibleIQ compares the action across its occurrences.
simple.summary: אָטַם (ʼâṭam) / H331 is traced through 1 Kings 6:4, Psalms 58:5, Proverbs 17:28, Proverbs 21:13 with source-language evidence and verse context.

definitions.full: H331. atam [ אטם ] verb shut, shut up (Mishna אטם , compare אוֺטֶם stoppage , Aramaic אֲטַם ; Arabic contract, stop , fortress ; Assyrian a‰amu , in list of headgear, etc. = turban ? Dl W, No. 155 ) — Qal Participle active אֹטֵם Prov 17:28 2 t.; passive אֲטֻמִים 1Kin 6:4 ; אֲטֻמוֺת Ezek 40:16 2 t.; — shut, stop , object lips Prov 17:28 ; ears 21:13 ; Isa 33:15 ; passive = closed (i.e. narrowed, narrowing , compare ᵑ6 in Co) א ׳חַלּוֺנוֺת Ezek 40:16 ; 41:16 , 26 ; compare אֲטֻמִים שְׁקֻפִים חַלּוֺנֵי 1Kin 6:4 . Hiph`il Imperfect id quod Qal יַאְטֵם Psa 58:5 (jussive with sense of indicative, compare Dr § 173 obs .) of adder, stopping ears, simile of wicked.
